In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the western foothills, in the cities of the southern wilderness, in the region where the descendants of Benjamin live, in the areas around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, shepherds will again count their sheep as the sheep walk past them.’ {That will surely happen because I,} Yahweh have said it.
Listen to this! A time is coming when I{, Yahweh} will do for the people of Israel and the people of Judah all the good things that I promised to do for them.
At that time I will appoint a righteous man who will be a descendant of King David. Throughout the land, he will do what is just and right.
At that time, I will rescue the people of Judah, and the people who live in Jerusalem will be safe. People will call their city, ‘Yahweh is the one who makes things right for us.’
This is also what {I,} Yahweh, say: ‘There will always be a descendant of King David to rule over the people of Israel.

There will also always be priests, who are descendants of Levi, standing in front of me to serve me. They will offer sacrifices that they completely burn on the altar, and they will burn grain offerings and present other sacrifices to me.’”
Then Yahweh gave {me,} Jeremiah {another} message. He said,
“This is what {I,} Yahweh, say: ‘I have set up the fixed order that governs the daytime and the nighttime, so that they always come at their proper times, and you certainly cannot annul that order.

In a similar way, you cannot annul the covenant that I made with King David, who served me, my promise that his descendants will always rule as kings. You also cannot annul my covenant with the descendants of Levi, who serve me as priests.

As no one can count the stars in the sky, and no one can measure the grains of sand along the seashore. In a similar way, I will give a huge number of descendants to King David, who serves me, and to the descendants of Levi, who serve me as priests.’”
Then Yahweh gave {me,} Jeremiah, another message. He said,

“You have surely noticed what these people are saying. They say, ‘Yahweh chose the two groups, the people {of Israel} and the people {of Judah}, but now he has rejected them.’ By saying this, they are despising my people, and they no longer regard the Israelites as a nation.
{However,} this is what I, Yahweh, say: ‘I will certainly not change my laws of nature that I have established to control the day and the night, the sky and the earth.

Just as surely as I have firmly established those laws of nature, I will never abandon the descendants of Jacob or the descendants of David, who served me. I will always choose rulers from among David’s descendants to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will cause them to prosper again, and I will act mercifully toward them.’”

King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came with his whole army and with the armies of all the kingdoms that he ruled, and they fought against Jerusalem and against all the other cities of Judah. At that time, Yahweh gave {me,} Jeremiah, this message. He said,

“{I am} Yahweh, the God whom you Israelites worship, and I am telling you to go to Zedekiah, the king of Judah, and tell him this. ‘Yahweh, says this: “I am about to enable the army of the king of Babylon to capture this city, and they will burn it down.

You will not escape from them. They will surely capture you and hand you over to the control of the king of Babylon. You will meet the king of Babylon in person and speak with him directly, and {then} they will take you to Babylon.’
But King Zedekiah, listen to what I, Yahweh, promise about you: ‘You will not die in battle.

You will die peacefully. {At your funeral} people will burn incense to honor you, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you. They will mourn for you, {crying out,} “We are very sad, our master!” This {will surely happen} because I myself have spoken it. This is what {I,} Yahweh, declare.’”
So {I,} Jeremiah the prophet, told all of this to King Zedekiah while I was in Jerusalem.

At that time the army of the king of Babylon was attacking Jerusalem and all the remaining cities of Judah, Lachish and Azekah. Because those were the only cities in Judah that had high walls around them that the Babylonians had not yet captured.
Yahweh gave {me,} Jeremiah, a message after King Zedekiah had made a solemn agreement with all the people who were in Jerusalem, that they must free their slaves.
{He decreed that} the people must free their Hebrew slaves, both the men and the women. No one was to keep a fellow Jew as a slave any longer.
So all the officials and the rest of the people who had agreed to this obeyed, and they freed their slaves.
But later they changed their minds. They forced the men and women whom they had freed to become their slaves again.
So Yahweh gave {me,} Jeremiah, this message. He said,
“{I,} Yahweh, the God whom you Israelites worship, say this. Long ago, when I rescued your ancestors from Egypt, where they were slaves, I made a solemn agreement with them. I told them this:

‘Every seventh year, each of you must free any fellow Hebrew who has sold himself to you and has served you for six years. You must let him go free.’ But your ancestors did not pay any attention to what I said.

Recently, you yourselves did what pleases me: you stopped doing what was wrong. Each of you promised to free your fellow Israelites, and you made a solemn agreement about this before me in my temple, the place that belongs to me.

But now you have disregarded what you solemnly promised and dishonored me. Each of you has taken back the male and female slaves whom you had freed to live where they desired, and you have forced them to be your slaves again.

Therefore, this is what {I,} Yahweh, say: ‘Because you have not obeyed me by each of you freeing your fellow Israelites, I will certainly now set you free—free to die in war, from disease, and from famine! I will make the people from all the kingdoms of the earth horrified when they see what happens to you.

I will cut apart the people who have disobeyed what I said in my solemn agreement and who did not do what they solemnly promised before me. To confirm that agreement, they cut a calf into two pieces and walked between the pieces.
{This includes} the officials of Judah and the officials of Jerusalem, the palace officials, the priests, and all the rest of the common people—everyone who walked between the pieces of the calf.
I will enable their enemies, who want to kill them, to capture them, and their enemies will kill them. Their dead bodies will become food for the birds and the wild animals.
I will enable the army of the king of Babylon to capture King Zedekiah of Judah and his officials. Although the king of Babylon and his army have left Jerusalem {for a short time}.

Know that I{, Yahweh,} am giving the command that will cause the army of Babylon to return to this city. They will attack it, capture it, and burn it down. And I will make sure that the cities of Judah are destroyed and no longer have anyone living in them.’” That is what Yahweh declares.
{Several years earlier,} when Jehoiakim, whose father was Josiah, was the king of Judah, Yahweh gave {me,} Jeremiah, this message. He said,
“Go to the place where the families of the Rechabite clan live. Invite them to my temple. {When they arrive,} take them into one of the side rooms and offer them wine.”
So I went to get Jaazaniah and his brothers and all his sons, who represented the Rechabite clan. Jaazaniah was the son of {another man named} Jeremiah and the grandson of Habazziniah.

I took them to the temple of Yahweh, {and we went} into the room where the sons of Hanan stayed. Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, was a prophet. That room was next to the room that the officials used, and it was above the room that belonged to Maaseiah the son of Shallum, who was the gatekeeper of the temple.
Then I set pitchers full of wine and some cups in front of them, and I said to them, “Drink some wine.”
They {refused} and said, “We do not drink wine, because our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us that we and our descendants must never drink wine.

He also told us that we must not build houses or sow seed or plant vineyards, nor own any of these things. But instead, we must always live in tents, so that we would live for many years in this land where we live as foreigners.
So we have obeyed everything that our ancestor Jonadab commanded us. We, our wives, our sons, and our daughters have never drunk wine.
We have not built houses to live in, and we do not have vineyards or fields or crops.
We have lived in tents, and we have obeyed everything that our ancestor Jonadab commanded us.

However, when King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and his army attacked this country, we said, ‘We must go to Jerusalem to escape from the Babylonian army and the Aramean army.’ So we are now living in Jerusalem.”
Then Yahweh gave {me,} Jeremiah, this message. He said,

“Go and tell the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem that this is what {I,} Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of Israel, say to them: ‘You refuse to accept my correction and pay attention to my messages’”. That is what Yahweh declares.

The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab have obeyed what their ancestor commanded them, so they do not drink wine to this day. I, however, have spoken to you people again and again, but you have not obeyed me.

I have sent all my servants the prophets to you again and again. They told you, “Each one of you must stop doing wicked things and do what is good. Stop worshiping other gods. Then you will live in the land that I gave to you and your ancestors.” Yet you did not pay attention to me or obey me.
The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab have obeyed the command that their ancestor gave them, but you people have refused to obey me.’

So this is what {I,} Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of Israel, say: ‘Know that I am going to bring on the people of Judah and everyone living in Jerusalem all the disasters that I threatened because I spoke to them, but they did not pay attention; I called out to them, but they did not respond.’”

Then {I,} Jeremiah, said to the Rechabite clan, “Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of Israel, says this: ‘Because you have obeyed the command of your ancestor Jonadab and have kept all his instructions and have done everything that he commanded you,
therefore Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of Israel, promises this: ‘There will always be descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab who will serve before me.’”
During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was the king of Judah, Yahweh spoke this message to {me,} Jeremiah. He said,

“Take a scroll and write on it all the messages that I have spoken to you about Israel and about Judah and about all the other nations. Write down everything that I have told you, from the time when Josiah was king until today.

It may be that the people of Judah will hear about all the disasters that I am planning to bring on them, each of them will stop behaving wickedly. If they do that, I will forgive them for their sinful behavior.”
So {I,} Jeremiah summoned Baruch son of Neriah, and while I spoke aloud all the messages that Yahweh had given me. Baruch wrote them on a scroll.
Then {I,}Jeremiah instructed Baruch, “The authorities have forbidden me to enter the temple of Yahweh.

You must go there {instead}. On a day when the people are abstaining from food, read aloud from the scroll the messages of Yahweh that I dictated to you, so that the people in Yahweh’s temple can hear them. Read them aloud also so that all the people of Judah who come there from their cities can hear them.

Perhaps they will humbly plead with Yahweh {that he would act mercifully toward them,} and each of them will stop behaving wickedly, because Yahweh is extremely angry with these people and has threatened that he will punish them severely.”
Baruch son of Neriah did everything that {I,} Jeremiah the prophet had commanded him {to do}. He read aloud from the scroll the messages of Yahweh at the temple of Yahweh.

During the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was the king of Judah, all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who had come to Jerusalem from the cities of Judah proclaimed a time of fasting before Yahweh.

So at the temple of Yahweh, Baruch read aloud from the scroll the messages that {I,} Jeremiah, {had given him}, so that all the people could hear them. He read them in the room that belonged to Gemariah son of Shaphan, the scribe. That room was in the upper courtyard, next to the entrance of the New Gate of the temple of Yahweh.
Micaiah, the son of Gemariah and the grandson of Shaphan, heard all the messages of Yahweh {that Baruch read} from the scroll.

Then he went down to the palace, into the room of the scribe, where all the king’s officials were sitting. {They were} Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Akbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the {other} officials.
Micaiah told them everything that he had heard when Baruch read aloud from the scroll to the people.

So all the officials sent Jehudi, the son of Nethaniah and the grandson of Shelemiah and the great-grandson of Cushi, to say to Baruch, “Bring us that scroll that you read aloud to the people, and come here.” So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and went to them.
They said to him, “Please sit down and read it to us.” So Baruch read it aloud to them.
When they heard all the messages, they became afraid, each person expressing this to their neighbor. They said to Baruch, “We must certainly report all these messages to the king.”
Then they asked Baruch, “Please tell us: How did you get all these messages? Did Jeremiah dictate them to you?”
Baruch answered them, “{Yes,} Jeremiah spoke all these messages aloud to me, and I wrote them on the scroll with ink.”
Then the officials said to Baruch, “You and Jeremiah must go and hide. Do not let anyone know where you are.”
The officials put the scroll in the room of Elishama the scribe. Then they went to the king in the courtyard and reported to him everything {that Baruch had read to them}.
So the king sent Jehudi to bring the scroll, and Jehudi brought it from the room of Elishama the scribe. Jehudi read it aloud to the king and to all the officials who were standing beside the king.
It was the ninth month, {the cold season,} so the king was sitting in the part of the palace where he lived during the winter, and in front of him {a fire} was burning in a pot {to keep him warm.}

Each time Jehudi finished reading three or four columns of the scroll, the king cut off that section with a scribe’s knife and threw it into the fire in the pot. He did this again and again, until the whole scroll had finished {burning} in the fire that was in the pot.
The king and all his officials who heard all these messages were not afraid, and they did not tear their clothes {to show that they were sorry for what they had done}.
And even though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he refused to pay attention to them.

Then the king commanded his son Jerahmeel, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and {me,} Jeremiah the prophet. But {they were unable to do that because} Yahweh had hidden us.
After King Jehoiakim burned the scroll that held the messages that Baruch had written down while {I,} Jeremiah spoke them aloud, Yahweh spoke this message to {me,} Jeremiah. Yahweh said,
“Get another scroll and write on it all the messages that were on the first scroll, the one that Jehoiakim the king of Judah burned.

Regarding Jehoiakim the king of Judah you must say, ‘Yahweh says this: “you burned this scroll and you rebuked Jeremiah for writing on it that the king of Babylon would certainly come and destroy this land and put an end to every person and animal in it.

So now {I,}Yahweh say this about you Jehoiakim king of Judah: ‘None of your descendants will rule this kingdom. {After you die,} people will throw your corpse out on the ground, where it will lie in the heat during the day and in the frost during the night.

{I,} Yahweh will punish you and your descendants and your officials because of the wicked things that you have all done. I will bring on you, and on everyone who lives in Jerusalem, and on all the people of Judah, every disaster that I warned you about, because none of you would pay attention to me.’”

So {I,} Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe. While I spoke aloud, Baruch wrote on it all the messages of the scroll that Jehoiakim the king of Judah had burned in the fire. I, Jeremiah also dictated many other similar messages, and Baruch added them to the scroll.
Zedekiah son of Josiah became the king of Judah, ruling in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim. Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, was the one who made Zedekiah king over the land of Judah.
verses.heading: King Zedekiah asks Jeremiah to pray

verses.text: But King Zedekiah, his palace officials, and the other people in the land refused to pay attention to the messages that Yahweh had given them through {me,} Jeremiah the prophet.
King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to {me,} Jeremiah the prophet with this request: “Please pray to Yahweh our God for us.”
At that time {I,} Jeremiah was still moving about freely among the people, because no one had yet put me in prison.

At that time the army of Pharaoh{, the king of Egypt} had marched out from Egypt. When the army of Babylonia who were surrounding Jerusalem, heard the report {about that army}, they stopped surrounding Jerusalem and marched away.
Then Yahweh gave this message to {me,} Jeremiah, the prophet. He said,

“{I,} Yahweh, the God of Israel say this: The king of Judah who sent {messengers} to you to ask me {what is going to happen}. Tell the king that {even though} the army of the king of Egypt, came to help him, they are about to return to their own land.
Then the Babylonian army will come back, attack this city, capture it, and burn it down.
I {also} say this {to you Israelites}: You should not deceive yourselves by thinking, ‘The Babylonian army has certainly left us for good.’ For they will not stay away.

Because even if you could defeat the entire Babylonian army that is fighting against you, so that only wounded men remained lying in their tents, those wounded men would get up and burn this city down.”
When the Babylonian army withdrew from Jerusalem because the army of Pharaoh was approaching,
verses.heading: Officials put Jeremiah in prison

verses.text: then, {I,} Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to the territory of Benjamin, in order to claim there the share of family property that belonged to me among my people.

However, when I reached the Gate of Benjamin, the officer in charge there, a man named Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah, arrested {me,} Jeremiah the prophet and accused me, saying, “You are deserting {us and going} to the soldiers of the Babylonian army!”
{I,} Jeremiah replied, “That is a lie! I am not deserting to the soldiers of the Babylonian army.” However, Irijah refused to pay attention to me. He arrested me and took me to the officials.
The officials were furious with {me,} Jeremiah. They {commanded the guards to} beat me and {then to} put me in the house of Jonathan the royal secretary, which they had turned into a prison.
They put {me,} Jeremiah into a dungeon cell, and I stayed there for a long time.

Then King Zedekiah sent {a servant} who brought me to the palace. There the king questioned me privately, “Is there any message from Yahweh?” {I,} Jeremiah answered, “Yes, there {is a message}. Yahweh will hand you over to the king of Babylon.”
Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, “I have not done anything wrong to you, or to your officials, or to these people. You had no reason to put me in prison.
Consider also your prophets, the ones who prophesied to you that the king of Babylon would not attack you or this land. Consider that their messages were not fulfilled.

So now, your majesty the king, please pay attention to me. Please grant the request that I am making to you: do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the royal secretary, so that I will not die there.”

So King Zedekiah gave orders that his men place me in the courtyard {of the palace} where the guards watched me. {He} also {ordered that} every day they bring me a loaf of bread from the street where the bakers worked, until there was no more bread anywhere in the city {because the Babylonian army besieged the city again.} So {I,} Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

{Four officials,} Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malkijah heard the messages that {I,} Jeremiah was delivering to all the people. I had been telling them that
verses.heading: Officials throw Jeremiah into a cistern

verses.text: Yahweh said that everyone who stayed in this city would die in war or from famine or from disease, but that everyone who left the city in order to surrender to the Babylonian army would stay alive. He said that they will escape with nothing, but the Babylonian soldiers will spare their lives.
Yahweh {also} said that he would certainly hand this city over to the army of the king of Babylon, and that army would capture it.

So those officials said to the king, “Please command your men to kill this man! Because by saying such things, he is making the soldiers who are still in this city lose their courage, and he is discouraging all the other people as well. This man does not want to help these people; he only wants to harm them.”
King Zedekiah answered, “All right, you may do with him whatever you want to; I cannot do anything to stop you.”

So those officials took {me,} Jeremiah and threw me into the cistern that belonged to Malkijah, a son of the king. That cistern was in the courtyard {of the palace} where the guards watched me, and they lowered me into it with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, so I sank down into the mud.

But Ebed Melech, a man from the land of Cush, served as an official in the king’s palace. He heard that the officials had put {me,} Jeremiah into the cistern. At that time the king was sitting and deciding people’s cases at the Benjamin Gate.
So Ebed Melech left the palace and spoke to the king. He said,

“Your majesty the king, these men have acted very wickedly in everything that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They threw him into a cistern, and he will starve to death down there, because there is no more food in the city.”
So the king commanded Ebed Melech, who was from the land of Cush, “Take thirty men from here with you, and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies.”

So Ebed Melech took the men with him and went into the palace, to a room underneath the storeroom. He got some worn-out rags and worn-out clothes from there, and he lowered them to Jeremiah in the cistern with ropes.
Then Ebed Melech, who was from the land of Cush, called down to {me,} Jeremiah, “Please put these worn-out rags and clothes under your armpits, to pad the ropes.” And I did that.
Then the men pulled {me,} Jeremiah up out of the cistern with the ropes. After that, I stayed in the courtyard {of the palace} where the guards watched me.

Later King Zedekiah sent men who brought {me,} Jeremiah the prophet, to him at the third entrance to the temple of Yahweh. The king said to me, “I want to ask you about something. Do not hide anything from me.”
verses.heading: Zedekiah questions Jeremiah again

verses.text: Jeremiah answered Zedekiah, “If I tell you, you will certainly kill me. And if I give you advice, you will not pay attention to me.”

So King Zedekiah secretly made a solemn promise to {me,} Jeremiah. He said, “As surely as Yahweh lives, the one who gave us the lives that we have, I will not kill you, and I will not hand you over to these men who are trying to kill you.”

Then {I,} Jeremiah, said to Zedekiah, “Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom the people of Israel worship, says this {to you}: ‘If you go out {and surrender} to the officials of the king of Babylon, you will stay alive, and no one will burn this city down, and you and your family will remain alive.

However, if you do not go out {and surrender} to the officials of the king of Babylon, then I will hand this city over to the Babylonian army, and they will burn it down, and you will certainly not escape from them.’”

King Zedekiah said to {me,} Jeremiah, “I am afraid of the Judeans who have deserted to the soldiers of Babylonia. The Babylonian soldiers may hand me over to those people of Judah, and those Judeans will abuse me.”
Jeremiah answered, “The Babylonian soldiers will not hand you over to them. Please obey what Yahweh is telling you through me. Then things will go well for you, and you will stay alive.
However, if you refuse to go out {and surrender}, this is what Yahweh has revealed to me.

Know for certain that men will bring out all the women who are still in the palace of the king of Judah, {and they will hand over} those women to the officials of the king of Babylon. Then those women will say to you: ‘Your friends, the men you trusted, misled you and got the better of you. Now you are completely helpless {it is as though} you are stuck in mud, and those men have abandoned you.’

Men will bring out all your wives and your sons to the Babylonian army, and you yourself will not escape from them. The king of Babylon will capture you, and the Babylonian soldiers will burn down this city.”
Then Zedekiah said to {me,} Jeremiah, “Do not let anyone at all know about what you told me; if you tell anyone, my officials may kill you.
If my officials find out that I have talked with you, they may come to you and say to you, ‘Please tell us what you and the king were talking about. If you tell us, we will not kill you.’
If that happens, then say to them, ‘I was pleading with the king not to send me back to the house of Jonathan, because I would die there.’”

Then all the officials came to {me,} Jeremiah and questioned me. I told them exactly what the king had commanded me to say. So they stopped questioning me, because no one had overheard what the king and I had said. to each other.

So {I,} Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard {of the palace} where the guards watched me. I stayed there until the day when the Babylonians captured Jerusalem and was there when the Babylonians captured it.
During the tenth month of the ninth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon led his whole army to Jerusalem. They surrounded the city and attacked it.
verses.heading: The Babylonians capture Jerusalem

verses.text: {About a year and a half later,} on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year that Zedekiah was king, the Babylonian soldiers broke through the wall of the city.

Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came into the city and sat down in the Middle Gate. They were Nergal Sarezer, Samgar Nebu, Sarsekim the chief officer, Nergal Sarezer the chief adviser, and all the other officials of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah the king of Judah and all his soldiers saw these officials, they ran away. During the night they left the city by way of the king’s garden, going out through the gate between the two walls. Then Zedekiah headed toward the Jordan River Valley.

But the Babylonian army chased after them and caught up with Zedekiah in the plains near the city of Jericho. They captured him and brought him to Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, who was at the city of Riblah in the land of Hamath. There Nebuchadnezzar judged Zedekiah for rebelling against him and decided how to punish him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon forced Zedekiah to watch as his soldiers killed Zedekiah’s sons. His soldiers also killed all the nobles of Judah.
Then the king ordered his men to gouge out Zedekiah’s eyes and to put bronze chains on him, so that they could take him to the city of Babylon.
The Chaldean soldiers also burned down the king’s palace and the houses of the people of Jerusalem, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem.

Then Nebuzaradan, the commander of the {king’s} bodyguards, took away to Babylon as captives the people who still remained in the city, along with those who had deserted to the king of Babylon and {most of} the other people who remained.

But Nebuzaradan, the commander of {the king of Babylon’s} bodyguards, allowed some of the very poor people, those who owned nothing, to stay in the land of Judah, and on that day he gave to them vineyards and fields {to take care of}.
Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had {previously} given orders to Nebuzaradan, the commander of his bodyguards, regarding {me,} Jeremiah. He said,
verses.heading: The Babylonians set Jeremiah free

verses.text: “Take Jeremiah and look after him. Do not harm him in any way. Instead, do for him whatever he asks you to do.”

So Nebuzaradan the commander of the bodyguards, Nebushazban the chief officer, Nergal Sharezer the king’s adviser, and all the other chief officers of the king of Babylon sent some of their men to get Jeremiah.

Those men sent and brought {me,} Jeremiah out of the courtyard {of the palace} where the guards watched me and handed me over to Gedaliah, who was the son of Ahikam and the grandson of Shaphan. Gedaliah was to take {me,} Jeremiah back to my own home. So I lived among my own people.
{Earlier,} while the guards were still keeping {me,} Jeremiah in the courtyard {of the palace}, Yahweh had given me this message. He said,

“Go to Ebed Melech, the man from the land of Cush, and tell him that Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom the Israelites worship, says this: ‘Pay attention! I am about to do to this city everything that I warned I would do. I will cause the people of this city to experience disasters; I will not enable this people to prosper. At that time you will see enemy soldiers destroy Jerusalem.
But at that time I will rescue you. I will not allow those people whom you are afraid of to conquer you.’ That is what Yahweh declares.
‘I will certainly rescue you. You will not die in war. You will escape with nothing except your own life, but you will remain alive, because you have trusted in me.’” That is what Yahweh declares.

Yahweh gave {me,} Jeremiah a message after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guards, had released me when I was in the town of Ramah {north of Jerusalem}where I and many other people from Jerusalem and {other places in} Judah had been sent after {the Babylonian soldiers} had fastened chains around our wrists. {They had brought us to Ramah because they planned} to take us to Babylon.
verses.heading: Nebuzaradan sets Jeremiah free

verses.text: The commander of the bodyguards took Jeremiah aside and said to him, “Yahweh your God said that he would bring this disaster on the people who live here in Jerusalem.

Now Yahweh has caused it to happen; he has done exactly what he said he would do. All this has happened to you people of Judah because you sinned against Yahweh and did not obey what he commanded you.

But today I have taken off the chains that were on your wrists, and I am setting you free. If you want to come with me to Babylon, then come, and I will take good care of you. But if you do not want to come with me to Babylon, then do not come. Look, the whole land is open to you. Go anywhere you think it is good and right to go.”

But before Jeremiah turned to leave, Nebuzaradan said to him, “Go back to Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam and the grandson of Shaphan, the man whom the king of Babylon has appointed to govern the cities of Judah. Live with him among the people. Or go anywhere else that you think it is right to go.” Then the commander of the bodyguards gave Jeremiah an allowance of food and a gift, and he let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam at the town of Mizpah, and he lived there with him among the people whom the Babylonians had allowed to remain in the land.

All the commanders of the groups of Judean soldiers who were still out in the open country, along with their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to govern the land. They also heard that the king had put in Gedaliah’s care the men, women, and children who were the poorest people in the land, those whom he had not taken away to Babylon as captives.
verses.heading: The people who remained gather to Gedaliah

verses.text: So those commanders went {to talk} to Gedaliah at Mizpah. {Those who went included} Ishmael the son of Nethaniah; Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah; Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth; the sons of Ephai from the town of Netophah; and Jezaniah, whose father was from the region of Maacah. Their men went with them.

Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam and the grandson of Shaphan, made a solemn promise to those commanders and their men. He said, “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Settle down in this land and serve the king of Babylon. If you do that, things will go well for you.

As for me, I will stay here at Mizpah in order to represent you before the {officials from} Babylonia whenever they come to {talk with} us. But you should {return to your towns and} harvest grapes to make wine, gather the fruit {that ripens in} the hot season, and pick olives {to make oil}. Store all of it in your jars, and live in the towns that you have taken for yourselves.”

Then all the Jews who were living in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the other countries also heard that the king of Babylon had allowed some of the people to remain in Judah, and that he had appointed Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam and the grandson of Shaphan, to govern them.

So all those Judeans came back from all the places where the Babylonians had scattered them. They came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah. There they harvested a very large amount of grapes and summer fruit.
{Some time later} Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the troops who were still out in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
verses.heading: Johanan warns Gedaliah about a plot

verses.text: They said to him, “Are you aware that Baalis, the king of the Ammonites, has sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to kill you?” But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan the son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah. He said, “Please let me go and kill Ishmael the son of Nethaniah. No one will find out who did it. You must not let him kill you! If he kills you, all the Judeans who have gathered around you will scatter, and the rest of the people of Judah will die.
But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said to Johanan the son of Kareah, “Do not do that because you are lying about Ishmael.”

In the seventh month {of that year}, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah and grandson of Elishama came to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam at Mizpah. Ishmael belonged to the royal family and had been one of the king’s chief officers. Ten men came with him. They all ate a meal together at Mizpah.
verses.heading: Ishmael murders Gedaliah

verses.text: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him got up and attacked Gedaliah the son of Ahikam and grandson of Shaphan with their swords, and Ishmael killed him. Gedaliah was the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed to govern the land.
Ishmael also killed all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah in Mizpah, along with the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
On the day after Ishmael killed Gedaliah, no one had yet found out what he had done.

Eighty men came from the cities of Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes, and cut themselves {to show that they were mourning}. They were carrying grain offerings and incense to bring to the temple of Yahweh {in Jerusalem}.
Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, and he wept continually as he walked along. When he met them, he said to them, “Come with me to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.”
When they had come into the middle of the city, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah and his men killed them and threw their bodies into a cistern.

However, ten of those men said to Ishmael, “Do not kill us because we have supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey that we have hidden in a field.” So Ishmael stopped and did not kill them along with their fellow Judeans.

The cistern which Ishmael’s {men} threw all the bodies of the men whom they had killed along with Gedaliah was the same one that King Asa’s {men} had dug so that {they would have water in the city} if the army of King Baasha of Israel would surround the city. The men of Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled that cistern with the bodies of the people they had killed.

Then Ishmael {and his men} captured all the rest of the people who were at Mizpah, including the king’s daughters and everyone else who still remained there. Nebuzaradan the commander of the king’s bodyguards had put all those people in the care of Gedaliah the son of Ahikam. Ishmael the son of Nethaniah took them as his captives and started off to cross over to the Ammonites.
Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the troops who were with him heard about all the evil things that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done.
verses.heading: Johanan rescues the captives

verses.text: So they took all their men and went to fight against Ishmael the son of Nethaniah. They found him at the large pool in Gibeon.
When all the people whom Ishmael had captured saw Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the troops who were with him, they were very glad.
All the people whom Ishmael had captured at Mizpah turned around and went over to Johanan the son of Kareah.
However, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight of his men, and he went to the Ammonites.

Then Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the troops who were with him gathered all the rest of the people whom they had rescued from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah. Ishmael had taken those people away from Mizpah after he killed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam. Among them were soldiers, women, children, and royal officials. Johanan brought them all back from Gibeon.
They set out and stayed at Geruth Kimham, which is near Bethlehem, because they intended to go on into Egypt.

They wanted to get away from the Chaldeans, because they were afraid of them. They were afraid {of what the Babylonian soldier would do} because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed to govern the land.

Then all the commanders of the troops, along with Johanan the son of Kareah and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah, and all the rest of the people, from the least important to the most important, came forward.
verses.heading: Jeremiah warns the people not to go to Egypt

verses.text: They said to {me,} Jeremiah the prophet, “Please do this thing we are requesting of you, and pray to Yahweh your God for us, for all of us who remain. Pray for us because formerly we were very many people, but as you can see, only a few of us have survived.
{Pray} so that Yahweh your God will tell us where we should go and what we should do.”

{I,} Jeremiah the prophet said to them, “I have heard you. I will indeed pray to Yahweh your God, just as you have asked me to do. Whatever Yahweh answers you, I will tell you; I will tell you everything he says.”
Then they said to Jeremiah, “May Yahweh himself be a truthful and reliable witness against us if we do not carefully do everything that Yahweh your God sends you to tell us.
Whether his answer pleases us or not, we will obey Yahweh our God, the one to whom we are sending you. If we obey Yahweh our God, then things will go well for us.”
Ten days later, Yahweh gave his message to {me,} Jeremiah.
So {I,} Jeremiah summoned Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the troops who were with him, and all the rest of the people, from the least important to the most important.
I said to them, “You sent me to Yahweh, the God whom we Israelites worship, to present your request to him, and this is what Yahweh says:

‘I am sad about the disaster that I caused you to suffer so you {should} change your mind and stay in this land, and if you do that then I will make you strong as a nation and I will not destroy you; I will settle you here permanently and I will not drive you out.

Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, the man whom you now fear. Do not be afraid of him’—this is what Yahweh declares—‘because I will be present with you in order to save you and in order to rescue you from him.
I will be merciful to you by causing the king of Babylon to act mercifully toward you, so that he will let you return to your own land.’
However, you may refuse to obey Yahweh your God and say that you will not stay in this land.

You may instead say that you will go to the land of Egypt, where you will not experience any war or hear the sound of a horn {signaling our soldiers to get ready for battle} or be hungry for food, and that you will live there.

If you say that, then listen to what Yahweh tells you, you people of Judah who remain. Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom we Israelites worship, says this: ‘If you insist on going to Egypt, and you go and live there as sojourners,

then you will experience there in the land of Egypt the very war that you are afraid of, and you will also suffer there the very famine that you worry about. You will certainly not avoid it by going to Egypt, and you will die there.

Every person who has decided to go to Egypt and live there as sojourners will die in war, or from famine, or from disease. Not one of them will survive or escape the disaster that I am about to bring on them.’

Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom we Israelites worship, says this: ‘I became extremely angry with the people who lived in Jerusalem, and I punished them severely. In the same way, I will become very angry with you and punish you severely when you go to Egypt. You will be an object of cursing and people will be horrified when they see what happens to you and you will be the thing by which people pronounce curses and you will be the object of people’s insults, and you will never see this place again.’
You people of Judah who remain, Yahweh has told you not to go to Egypt. You should clearly understand that I am warning you today.
{I am warning you} that you were insincere when you requested me to pray to Yahweh our God for you and to tell you everything that Yahweh our God would say, and you said that you would do it.
Today I have told you what he said, but you have not obeyed Yahweh your God; you have not obeyed anything that he sent me to tell you.
So now, you should clearly understand that you will die in war or from famine or from disease in the place where you want to go and live as sojourners.”
{I,} Jeremiah told all the people everything that Yahweh their God had sent me to tell them. When I finished
verses.heading: The people of Judah refuse to obey Yahweh and go to Egypt

verses.text: Azariah the son of Hoshaiah and Johanan the son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to {me} Jeremiah, “You are lying! Yahweh our God did not send you to tell us that we must not go to Egypt and live there.
Rather {we think that it is} Baruch the son of Neriah, who is urging you to speak against us so that the Babylonian soldiers will seize us in order to kill us or take us away to Babylon as captives.”
So Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the troops and all the people refused to obey what Yahweh commanded them; they would not stay in the land of Judah.

Instead, Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the troops took away all the people of Judah who still remained. These were the people who had come back to live in the land of Judah from all the nations where their enemies had driven them.

{They took} the men, the women, and the children, and the king’s daughters and every person whom Nebuzaradan the commander of the king’s bodyguards had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam and the grandson of Shaphan. They took {me,} Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch the son of Neriah as well.
They went into the land of Egypt, because they refused to obey what Yahweh told them. They traveled as far as the city of Tahpanhes.
There in Tahpanhes, Yahweh spoke a message to Jeremiah. He said,
verses.heading: Yahweh warns that Nebuchadnezzar will conquer Egypt

verses.text: “Pick up some large stones and bury them in the clay under the bricks of the pavement at the entrance to the palace of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes. Do this while the men from Judah are watching you.

Then tell those men that this is what I, Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of Israel, say to them: ‘I am about to send for Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, the man who does my work, and I will bring him here. I will place his throne over these stones that I have told Jeremiah to bury here, and he will rule as king from that place. He will spread out his royal tent over these stones {to show that he now rules over Egypt}.

He will come and attack the people of the land of Egypt. He will kill the people whom I have decided must die, his soldiers will capture the people whom I have decided must become captives, and they will kill with their swords the people whom I have decided must die in war.

Nebuchadnezzar’s soldiers will burn down the temples where the Egyptians worship their idols. {But before} they burn the temples, they will take away their idols as plunder. He will take complete control of the land of Egypt without any difficulty just as a shepherd easily controls his garment when he wraps it around himself, and then Nebuchadnezzar will leave that land safely, because no one there will harm him.

Nebuchadnezzar’s soldiers will tear down the sacred stone pillars at Beth Shemesh, the place in the land of Egypt where the people worship the sun, and he will burn down the temples where the Egyptians worship their gods.’”

This is the message that Yahweh gave to {me,} Jeremiah for all the Jewish people who were living in the land of Egypt, that is, those who were living in the cities of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis, and in the region of Pathros {in southern Egypt}. Yahweh said this:
verses.heading: Yahweh warns the Judeans in Egypt about their idol worship

verses.text: “This is what {I,} Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of you Israelites say: ‘You yourselves saw all the terrible things that I caused {the people in} Jerusalem and all the other cities of Judah to experience. Look at them today: they lie in ruins, and hardly anyone lives in them.

{That happened} because of the evil things that the people there did. They made me very angry by going and burning incense and worshiping other gods that they had {previously} not known about. Neither they nor you nor your ancestors had {previously} known those gods.
Again and again I sent all my servants the prophets to you, and I told them to plead with you not to do this detestable thing that I hate.
However, your ancestors did not pay any attention {to my prophets}. They refused to stop their wicked behavior, and they would not stop burning incense to other gods.
So I showed them how extremely angry I was, and I punished {the people in} the cities of Judah and on the streets of Jerusalem. Those places became an empty ruin, and they are still like that today.’

So now Yahweh, the god who commands the heavenly armies, the God of you Israelites, says this: ‘Do you not realize that {because of} what you are doing you are causing yourselves to experience these terrible disasters with the result that {soon} you will cause there to be no more men, women, children or infants left among you {who have come here to Egypt from Judah}?

You are making me angry by burning incense to other gods you have made here in the land of Egypt, where you have come to live. The result {if you continue to do this} will be that you destroy yourselves, and that people in every nation on the earth will use your name when they curse someone and will despise you.

You have forgotten {how I punished} your ancestors for the wicked things they did, and {how I punished} the kings of Judah and queens of Judah for the wicked things they did, and you and your wives for the wicked things that you did in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem.
To this day you have not humbled yourselves or revered me. You have not obeyed all my laws that I gave to you and to your ancestors.’
So Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom you Israelites worship, says this: ‘I have firmly decided to bring disaster on you and to destroy all the people of Judah.
verses.heading: Yahweh promises to destroy the Judeans who fled to Egypt

verses.text: I will take away the people of Judah who survived, the ones who were determined to go to the land of Egypt and live there. All of them will perish there in the land of Egypt, from the least important of them to the most important. They will die in war or from famine. People will make them an object of cursing and people will be horrified when they see what happens to them and they will be the thing by which people pronounce curses and they will be the object of people’s insults.
I will punish the people who are living in the land of Egypt just as I punished the people of Jerusalem: by war, by famine, and by disease.

None of the people of Judah who survived and came to live in the land of Egypt will get away or stay alive to return to the land of Judah, even though they long to go back and live there. Only a very few of them will escape and return.’”

Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women who were standing there in a large crowd, and all the people who were living in the region of Pathros in the land of Egypt, answered {me,} Jeremiah. They said,
verses.heading: The people refuse to stop worshiping the Queen of Heaven

verses.text: “You are saying that Yahweh gave messages to you to tell us on his behalf, {but} we will not pay any attention to your messages.

We will certainly do everything that we said we would do. We will burn incense to the goddess whom we call the Queen of Heaven, and we will pour out wine offerings to her, just as we and our ancestors and our kings and our officials did in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. At that time we had plenty of food, we prospered, and we did not experience difficult things.

However, from the time that we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out wine offerings to her, we have lacked nearly everything, and many of our people have died in war and from famine.”

Then {the women said,} “When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out wine offerings to her, our husbands certainly knew that we were making cakes that resembled her idol to offer her and that we were pouring out wine offerings to her, and they agreed to it.”
Then {I,} Jeremiah spoke to all the people, to the men and to the women and to everyone who had answered him in that way. I said,
verses.heading: Jeremiah answers the people

verses.text: “Yahweh certainly did not forget the incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, both you and your ancestors and your kings and your officials and all the people of the land. Yahweh remembered what you did and kept thinking about it.

Finally Yahweh could no longer endure your evil deeds and the detestable things that you were doing. So he caused your land to become a place of ruins and a horrifying place, a land that people mention when they pronounce curses, a land where no one lives, just as it still is today.

Because you burned incense {to idols} and sinned against Yahweh, and did not obey what Yahweh said to you and did not live according to all his commands, therefore you have experienced {all} these disasters, as is clearly evident today.”
Then {I,} Jeremiah said to all the people, including all the women, “All you people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt, listen to this message from Yahweh.

Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of Israel, says this {to you men of Judah}: ‘You and your wives have said that you would certainly {continue} to do what you vowed by burning incense and pouring out wine to {the goddess whom you call} the Queen of Heaven and you have done what you said. {Since you insist, go ahead and} keep your vows! Do exactly what you vowed to do!’

So now, all you people of Judah who are living in the land of Egypt, pay attention to this message from Yahweh. He says, ‘I have solemnly sworn by my own great name that never again will anyone from Judah anywhere in the land of Egypt use my name to make a promise by saying, “{I will do it as surely as} Lord Yahweh lives.”

I am watching over these people, intending to bring disaster on them and not good things. Nearly all the people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will die in war or from famine, until none of them are left.

Only a few people will survive the war and return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah. Then all the people of Judah who survived and came to live in the land of Egypt will know whose words came true, mine or theirs.
I will give you a sign’—this is what Yahweh declares—‘that I will indeed punish you here in this place, so that you may know that my messages about bringing disaster on you will certainly come true.’

Yahweh says this: ‘I am about to allow the men who want to kill Pharoah Hophra, the king of Egypt, to capture him just as I allowed Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, who wanted to kill Zedekiah, the king of Judah, {to have his soldiers} capture him.’”

During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was the king of Judah, Baruch son of Neriah was writing on a scroll the messages that {I,} Jeremiah the prophet was speaking aloud to him. At that time I gave Baruch this message. I said,
verses.heading: Yahweh gives a message to Baruch

verses.text: “Baruch, this is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says to you:

You said, ‘Terrible things {are happening} to me. Yahweh has caused me to experience things that have caused me to be sorrowful in addition to the things he caused me to experience that are painful. I am exhausted from my groaning and I am unable to rest.’

{Yahweh told me} I must tell you this {in response}: ‘I Yahweh say this: {Like} a builder who builds a house and then tears it down, I myself established this nation, {but now} I am destroying it and {like} a farmer who plants a crop and then uproots it I myself settled this people in their land, but now I am removing them from it. I will do this throughout all the earth.

As for you, I am surprised that you are seeking great things for yourself. Do not seek them, because I am about to bring a terrible disaster on everyone. That is what I, Yahweh, declare. However, wherever you go, I will let you escape with nothing except your own life, but you will remain alive there.’”
This is the message that Yahweh gave to {me,} Jeremiah the prophet about the {other} nations.
verses.heading: Yahweh gives messages about the nations

verses.text: {Yahweh gave this message} about Egypt, regarding the army of Pharaoh Neco the king of Egypt. That army was at the city of Carchemish beside the Euphrates River when {the army of} Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon defeated it. {This happened} during the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was the king of Judah.
verses.heading: Yahweh gives a message about Egypt

verses.text: {Yahweh said, “You soldiers of Egypt,} get your small shields and your large shields ready, and march out to fight the battle!
Harness the horses; you horsemen, mount them and take your places. Put on your helmets, sharpen your spears, and put on your armor!

This is what I see: the soldiers of Egypt are panicking, and they are retreating. Their enemies are beating down their warriors. They run away as fast as they can, and they never turn back to face their enemies, because enemies surround them on every side and they greatly fear them.” This is what Yahweh declares.
“The fastest runners will not get away, and the warriors will not escape. In the north, beside the Euphrates River, they will stumble, and their enemies will kill them.
{Look at} who this is that is rising up {and covering the land} like the Nile River, like its streams when their waters surge {at flood stage}!

{It is the army of} Egypt that is rising up {and covering the land} like the water of the Nile River when it floods and covers the land. The Egyptians boast that they will advance and cover the whole earth, and that they will destroy cities and the people who live in them.
You {riders of} horses, charge {into the battle}! You chariot {drivers}, drive furiously! All you warriors from Cush and Put, who carry your shields, you warriors from Lydia who shoot arrows, come!

{You need to know that,} that is the time when {I,} Lord Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies; will pay my enemies back for what they have done. {The soldiers from Babylon} will use their swords to kill so many of my enemies that they will finally have killed all that they wanted to kill. {The Egyptian soldiers who will die} in the north, beside the Euphrates River, {will be like} a sacrifice to {me}, Lord Yahweh the Commander of the heavenly armies.
You people of Egypt, go to the region of Gilead to get help! In vain I have done many things to try to help you, {and because you stubbornly refuse to obey me} nothing can help you {now}.

{People in} the {other} nations will hear {how I Yahweh have caused} enemy soldiers to disgrace you. {People everywhere on} earth have heard you crying out. {Your} warriors will stumble over each other, and they will all fall down together.”
This is the message that Yahweh spoke to {me,} Jeremiah the prophet about how Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon would come and attack the land of Egypt.

{Yahweh said,} “Announce this in Egypt, and proclaim it in the cities of Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. Tell the people there, ‘Take your positions and get ready {to fight}, because your enemies will kill everyone around you in battle.’
Yahweh will certainly destroy your soldiers. They will not be able to resist their enemies, because I Yahweh will defeat them.

I, Yahweh will make many of your soldiers fall; indeed, they will collide with one another as they flee. They will say {to each other}, ‘Get up! Let us go back to our own people, back to the land where we were born, so that we can escape from the enemies who are killing us!’
There {in Egypt} people will say, ‘Pharaoh the king of Egypt boasts loudly; {but when} he had an opportunity {to defeat our enemies}, our army failed.’

The King, whose name is Yahweh the commander of the heavenly armies, declares this: “As {surely as} I live, an enemy king’s army will certainly come {to fight against the army of Egypt}. That king’s army will be {extremely powerful as though it were as tall} as Mount Tabor which towers over mountains {around it}, or {as high} as Mount Carmel which towers over the Mediterranean Sea.

You people who live in Egypt, pack your possessions that you can carry, because your enemies will take you away as captives. They will ruin the city of Memphis completely; they will burn it, and no one will live there anymore.
Egypt is {like} a very beautiful young cow, but the army of a powerful king} from the northeast will surely come to attack it, {like} a horsefly {bites a cow}.

The foreign soldiers {from other countries} whom the Egyptians hired will become like calves that farmers fatten in a stall. They also will turn around and flee together; they will not stand {and fight}, because it will be a day when there will be disaster in Egypt, the time when {I, Yahweh} will punish them.

{The soldiers of} Egypt will flee, making only a faint sound, like a snake slithering away. Their enemies will advance with a great army; they will come against Egypt carrying axes, as woodcutters do.”

Yahweh, declares this: “Those enemy soldiers will bring down the soldiers {of Egypt} as though they were woodcutters and the Egyptian soldiers were an immense forest of trees that cannot be explored. {The enemy soldiers will be able to kill the numerous Egyptian soldiers} because their soldiers will be more numerous than a swarm of locusts; which no one is able to count.
The people of Egypt will be ashamed, {because} Yahweh will allow the people from the northeast to conquer them.”

Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom the Israelites worship, says this: “Pay attention! I am about to punish Amon, the god whom the people of the city of No worship. I will also punish Pharaoh, and Egypt, and the other gods that the Egyptians worship, and their kings. I will punish Pharaoh and everyone who trusts in him.

I will let their enemies capture them, the people who want to kill them, that is, Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon and his officials. However, after that, people will live {in Egypt again} as they did long ago.” That is what Yahweh, declares.

{Yahweh says,} “As for you people of Israel who serve me, do not be at all fearful, because I will surely save you and bring you back from distant places, and I will bring your descendants home from the land where others have taken them as prisoners. You people of Israel will return and live peacefully and safely again, and no nation will cause you to be afraid.

You people of Israel who serve me, do not be afraid, because I am with you {to help you}.”— This is what Yahweh declares.—“I will completely destroy all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not completely destroy you. I will discipline you fairly, but I will certainly not let you go without any punishment.”
Yahweh gave this message to {me,} Jeremiah the prophet, about the people of Philistia. {He gave it to me} before the Egyptian army attacked and captured the city of Gaza.
verses.heading: Yahweh gives a message about Philistia

verses.text: This is what Yahweh says: “Look! An army is coming from the north, that will cover the land like a flood. Those soldiers will overrun the land and everything in it, including every city and all the people who live there. Everyone who lives in the land will cry out and wail loudly.

When the people hear the sound of the galloping hooves of the enemy’s stallions, and the enemy’s chariots rattling and their wheels rumbling, the fathers will not even turn back to rescue their own children, because they will be so afraid.

{That will happen} because the time will have come when {I,} Yahweh will destroy all the people of Philistia and will kill every one of them who could still help the cities of Tyre and Sidon. I will destroy the people of Philistia, those who survive along the seacoast, whose ancestors came {long ago} from the island of Crete.

The people of Gaza will shave their heads bald to show that they are mourning. {I, Yahweh will allow enemy soldiers} to destroy the city of Ashkelon and all the people who remain in their valley. You people of Ashkelon who survive will go on cutting yourselves to show how deeply you grieve.”
{The people of Philistia say,} ‘Oh Yahweh, we wish that you would {make our enemies stop killing us} with their swords! Make them put their swords back into their sheaths and keep them there!’

{But I, Yahweh, say,} It would not be right for {your enemies’ swords} to stay in their sheaths, because Yahweh has commanded your enemies {to do something more}. He intends to tell them to attack {the people living in} the city of Ashkelon and {in the other cities} along the coast.”

This is what Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom the Israelites worship, says about Moab: “Terrible things will happen to the town of Nebo; {soon} enemy soldiers will ruin it! They will capture the town of Kiriathaim, and its people will be humiliated. the high wall around their city will be ruined, and {its people} will become ashamed.

No one will boast about Moab anymore. In the city of Heshbon their enemies are making plans to harm them. {Those enemies say,} ‘Come, let us destroy Moab so that it is no longer a nation.’ You people of the town of Madmen, they will silence you as well; enemy armies will chase after you.
The people of the town of Horonaim will cry out. {They will be wailing when their town} is completely destroyed!
{I} will destroy the nation of Moab, {and even} its little children will be distressed and cry.
They will weep bitterly as they ascend the steep path up to Luhith. Their enemies will hear {others wailing} their enemies will hear them crying out in anguish over the destruction.
Run away! Save your lives! You will barely survive, and you will have nothing left, out in the wilderness.

You people of Moab trusted in what you had accomplished and in the wealth you had stored up, so enemies will capture you as well. They will carry the idol of your god Chemosh away to a distant land, and they will take his priests and his officials along with it.

A destroying army will attack every city {in Moab}, and none of them will escape. {That army} will ruin the cities in the valley and destroy the cities on the plateau, because {I,} Yahweh, have said that this will happen.
Help the people of Moab get away quickly, because they must escape! Their cities will become an empty wasteland, and no one will live in them.
{I,} Yahweh will curse anyone who will not eagerly do what I desire. I will curse anyone who refrains from using his sword to kill those those {who are in Moab}.

The people of Moab have lived securely ever since they first became a nation. No enemy has captured them and taken them away to another country. So they have not changed. They are {like} wine that people have left undisturbed {in a container to ferment} but not removed from its dregs and placed in another container and which therefore remains unchanged in taste and smell.

So listen!”—Yahweh declares this—“The time is coming when I will send enemies against the people of Moab. Those enemies will destroy Moab and get rid of its people {like} people pouring wine out {on the ground} and then smashing the wine jars.
Then the people of Moab will feel ashamed of {their idol} Chemosh, just as the people of Israel felt ashamed of {their idol} at Bethel that they had trusted in.
{You people of Moab}, you should not boast saying, ‘We are mighty warriors, and we are brave men who are ready for battle!’

Enemies will devastate the country of Moab and attack its cities, and they will slaughter its finest young men. I am the King, and my name is Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies. That is what I declare.
Moab will be destroyed very soon!
All you {people who live in nations} near Moab, all of you who know how famous Moab is, should mourn for Moab, and say, ‘How completely Moab’s mighty rule has ended’

You people who live in the city of Dibon, stop being proud because people have honored you, come down and sit on the dry, parched ground, because the army that destroys Moab will attack your city and tear down the high walls that protect you.
You people who live in the city of Aroer, stand beside the road and watch. Ask the men and the women who are running away to save their lives; ask them, ‘What has happened?’
{Enemies of} the people of Moab have disgraced them, and they are dismayed. Weep and cry out loudly! Announce along the Arnon River that {enemies} have devastated Moab.
I am going to punish the cities {in Moab that are} on the plateau: Holon, Jahaz, and Mephaath,
Dibon, Nebo, and Beth Diblathaim,
Kiriathaim, Beth Gamul, and Beth Meon,
Kerioth, and Bozrah. I am punishing every city in the land of Moab, both the towns that are far away and the ones that are nearby.
{I, Yahweh} will end the powerful reign of Moab; {it will be as though} Moab will have a broken arm”—That is what Yahweh declares.

“{You people of Moab} have exalted yourselves against {me,} Yahweh, so {now} I will cause you all to {stagger like} drunken people. {You people of} Moab will wallow in your own vomit and people will laugh at you.
You people of Moab, you ridiculed the people of Israel. You treated them as though they were thieves. Every time you spoke about them, you shook your head {to show your scorn}.
You people who live in Moab, leave your cities and go live in the cliffs. Be like doves that make their nests in the entrances of caves.
We have {all} heard how proud the people of Moab are. They are extremely arrogant and they think they are better than everyone else.
I, {Yahweh} surely know”—Yahweh declares this—“how insolently they boast, but their boasting is empty, and they will never accomplish what they claim.
So I will wail for the people of Moab; I will cry out for everyone who lives there, and I will moan for the people of the city of Kir Hareseth.

You people of the city of Sibmah, I will weep for you even more than I did for the people of Jazer. You have many vineyards. The branches of your vines extend all the way to the sea and reach all the way to the sea of Jazer. Now, however, a destroying army will ruin the fruit that ripens in the summer and the grapes you would have harvested.

No one is glad or shouts for joy anymore in the orchards and fields of Moab. I have stopped the grape juice from flowing from the winepresses. People will not shout joyfully as they tread on the grapes; people will shout, but they will not be shouting joyfully.

People will cry out loudly from the city of Heshbon to the town of Elealeh to the village of Jahaz, from the city of Zoar as far as the town of Horonaim and the village Eglath Shelishiyah. Even the water at the stream of Nimrim will dry up.
I, {Yahweh,} will put a stop to everyone in Moab who offers sacrifices at the altars on the hilltops and who burns incense to their gods.” That is what Yahweh declares.

“So I{, Yahweh,} lament for the people of Moab like {the sound of a funeral song that someone plays on} a flute. Yes I lament for the people of the city of Kir Hareseth like {the sound of a funeral song that someone plays on} a flute. Therefore the wealth they have gained will perish.
Every man there will shave his head bald and cut off his beard {to show they are mourning}. They will all slash their hands, and wear sackcloth around their waists {to show that they are mourning}.

On every rooftop in Moab and in all its public squares, people there will be people who are mourning, because I {Yahweh} will have destroyed the nation of Moab like someone smashes an {old} jar that no one wants {any more}.” This is what Yahweh declares.

“The people of Moab will be greatly dismayed and will wail! The people of Moab will turn away because they are ashamed! Moab will become a nation that people ridicule. The people in nearby countries will be horrified about what has happened there.”
This is what Yahweh says: “Know that an enemy army will suddenly rush down and attack Moab by surprise, like an eagle swooping down to attack {its unsuspecting prey}.
Enemies will capture Kerioth and seize its fortresses. On that day the soldiers of Moab will feel afraid, like a woman who is giving birth.
I, {Yahweh,} will destroy Moab so that it is no longer a nation, because its people boasted against {me,} Yahweh.
Terrible things are going to happen to you people who live in Moab.” This is what Yahweh declares.

Anyone who runs away from the terror will fall into a pit, and anyone who climbs out of the pit will step into a trap, because I will bring on the people of Moab the year when I punish them.” This is what Yahweh, declares.

“The people who are running away will stop exhausted in the shadows of the walls of the city of Heshbon, because the city will be on fire. A fire will burn from the midst of the territory where King Sihon once ruled. That fire will burn the foreheads of the people of Moab, yes {it will burn} the heads of those people who loudly boast.

Terrible things will happen to you, people of Moab! You who worship the god Chemosh will perish, because enemies have taken your sons away as captives, and they have taken your daughters away as captives too.

Yet in the future I will restore the fortunes of the people of Moab and bring them back to their land. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.” That is the end of the message about how Yahweh will judge Moab.

This is what Yahweh says about the people of Ammon: “The Israelites certainly have descendants who can inherit their land, and they certainly have heirs. So the king of Ammon had no right to seize the territory of the tribe of Gad, and his people had no right to settle in the towns there.

So listen! The time is coming when I will send an army shouting its battle cry against Rabbah, the city of the Ammonites. That city will become nothing but a heap of rubble, and enemy soldiers will burn down the villages around it. Then the Israelites will take back their land from the people who took it away from them. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.

You people of Heshbon, wail loudly, because enemies have ruined the town of Ai! You people who live in the villages around Rabbah, cry out! Put on rough clothing to show that you are mourning, and weep, and run back and forth inside the walls, because enemies will take your king away to another country, and they will take his priests and his officials away as well.

You rebellious people of Ammon, you have no reason to boast about your valleys, about how fertile and productive your valley is. You trust in the wealth you have stored up, and you say, ‘No one will dare to attack me!’

Listen! I am about to terrify you, and every nation around you will frighten you. I, the Lord Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, declare this. Your enemies will drive you out, and each of you will run straight ahead, and no one will gather your scattered people together again.
Yet later on I will restore the fortunes of the people of Ammon and bring them back to their land. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”

This is what Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says about the people of Edom: “The region of Teman no longer has any wise people! The people who used to understand things can no longer advise anyone, and the wisdom they once had has become useless.
You people who live in Dedan, run away! Turn back! Go and hide yourselves in deep caves, because I am bringing disaster on the descendants of Esau at the time when I punish them.
When people harvest grapes, they always leave a few grapes on the vines. When thieves come during the night, they steal only as much as they want.

However, I myself will take everything away from the descendants of Esau; I will expose every place where they hide, so that they will not be able to hide from me at all. I will destroy their children, their relatives, and their neighbors, and the people of Edom will no longer exist.
You men of Edom will die, so leave your orphaned children with me, and I will keep them alive, and your widows can trust me to take care of them.”

This is what Yahweh says: “Listen! Even people who did not deserve to suffer my punishment must certainly suffer it. So I will certainly not treat you people of Edom as though you were innocent. I will punish you severely.

I have solemnly promised, swearing by my own name, that I will completely ruin the city of Bozrah. People will shudder in horror when they see it, they will insult it, and they will use its name when they curse others. All the towns that belong to it will remain ruins forever. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”
I, Jeremiah, have heard a message from Yahweh. He has sent a messenger to the nations to tell them, “Gather your armies together and attack Edom! Get ready to go to war!”
Yahweh says to the people of Edom, “Listen! I am making you the least important of all the nations, and everyone will despise you.

You have terrified other people, and that has fooled you; you have become very proud, because you live in caves in the rocky cliffs and you occupy the highest hills. Yet even if you build your homes as high up as an eagle builds its nest, I will bring you down from there. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.
What happens to Edom will horrify everyone. People who travel past it will gasp in shock, and they will hiss to show their scorn at how badly enemies have ruined the land.

Yahweh says, “I completely destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them, and I will destroy Edom in the same way. After that, no one will live in Edom at all; not even a traveler will stay there for a while.”

Listen! An enemy will suddenly attack the people of Edom while they feel safe in their land, just as a lion comes up out of the thick bushes along the Jordan River and attacks a flock grazing in a good pasture. In an instant I will chase the people of Edom out of their land, and I will put whichever leader I choose in charge of them. No one is equal to me, and no one can take me to court. No ruler anywhere can stand against me.”

So listen to what Yahweh has decided to do to the people of Edom, to what he has planned to do to those who live in Teman: Enemies will drag the Edomites away, even the youngest and weakest among them, and Yahweh will turn their homeland into a wasteland.
When the people of Edom fall in battle, the noise will be so loud that the earth will shake. People as far away as the Sea of Reeds will hear the people of Edom crying out.

Look! An enemy army will swoop down on the city of Bozrah like an eagle that swoops down and spreads its wings over its prey. On that day the brave soldiers of Edom will feel such terror that they will writhe like a woman suffering labor pains.

This is what Yahweh says about the city of Damascus: “The people of the cities of Hamath and Arpad feel ashamed, because they have heard bad news about Damascus. They have lost all their courage; they are as anxious and restless as the sea during a storm, and they cannot calm down.
The people of Damascus have become weak; they have turned to run away, and they tremble with fear. They suffer great anguish and pain, like a woman who is giving birth to a child.
How sad it is that the people have not abandoned that famous city, the town that once made me glad!
So enemies will kill her young men in the open squares of the city, and on that day they will kill all her soldiers. That is what I, Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, declare.
I will set the walls of Damascus on fire, and that fire will completely burn up the fortresses that King Ben Hadad built.”

This is what Yahweh says about the people of Kedar and about the kingdoms of Hazor, which King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon attacked: “You soldiers, get ready and go attack the people of Kedar! Destroy those tribes who live in the desert to the east!

Those soldiers will seize the tents and the flocks of those people; they will carry off for themselves their tent curtains, all their goods, and their camels. People will shout at them, ‘Terrible things are happening to us from every direction!’
